summary:
The Go prototype now follows all twelve §9 rulings on darwin-arm64 and in Linux containers. Four needed code changes, six already conformed (each now has a native test), and K7 and K12 needed only a statement. Windows has not been run.

Your starting positions held up. K2 and K3 were real gaps. K1, K4, K5 and K10's SIGTERM path already conformed. K10 also needed SIGHUP and panic handling. There was one gap you hadn't listed, in K6.

| Ruling | Result | Proof |
|---|---|---|
| K1 | already conformed | `TestK1ControlCharactersInIdentity`, selftest `agent.k1_controls_replaced` |
| K2 | **changed**: `profile.go` rejects control characters in `name`, `id`, `alias`, `host`, `account` and labels with SCHEMA_INVALID; `key_path` names the key and the value is never echoed. `[meta]` is still tolerated. | `TestK2ControlCharactersInValues`, selftest `profile.k2_*`. Before the fix: exit 0 with the canary on stdout. |
| K3 | **changed**: `frame.go` / `probe.go` report a close before any response byte as AGENT_UNAVAILABLE; EOF after one or more bytes is still AGENT_PROTOCOL_ERROR. | `TestK3EOFClassification`, selftest `agent.k3_*` |
| K4 | already conformed | `TestK4FailureFrameShape`, selftest `agent.k4_*` |
| K5 | already conformed | `TestK5MetaState`, selftest `run.k5_meta_state` |
| K6 | **changed**: `run_unix.go` rewritten (details below) | selftest `run.k6_*`; with the old `run_unix.go` the same check fails (exit 12, want 13) |
| K7 | statement: a `.`/empty PATH match is refused with exit 127 | none needed |
| K8 | already conformed | `TestInvalidUTF8ArgBytes`, selftest `run.k8_invalid_utf8_argv_bytes` |
| K9 | already conformed | `TestK9SelectionAfterFilterEdit`, selftest `tui.k9_*` |
| K10 | **changed**: `main.go` (new `runTUI`) and `tui.go` | three real-pty tests (panic exits 1, SIGHUP exits 129, hangup with no signal exits 129) and selftest `tui.k10_*`. Before: SIGHUP killed the process and left the terminal unrestored. |
| K11 | already conformed: one static file per target, no sidecars, no extraction | selftest `k11.no_writes_no_sidecars` |
| K12 | statement: plain-text output, same exit codes | none needed |

**K6 change.** The old design kept the child in heimdall's process group when heimdall started as a background job. After `fg`, it then dropped an explicit `kill -INT <heimdall pid>`. Now the child always gets its own process group, and every signal heimdall receives is forwarded exactly once. A 50 ms watcher hands the terminal to the child whenever heimdall's group is in the foreground, and job-control stops are mirrored without taking the terminal after `bg`.

**K10 detail.** On macOS, Bubble Tea treats input EOF as a silent stop, so a terminal hangup without SIGHUP left the picker running. A small input wrapper now maps EOF/EIO to 129; without it the hangup test fails.

**Tests and build:**
- Native: `go test ./...` exit 0 on darwin-arm64, and exit 0 for every package in linux/arm64 and linux/amd64 (emulated) containers.
- `go vet` exit 0 on all four targets. Windows test compile exit 0. `go.mod` unchanged.
- `build.sh` exit 0 for all 4 targets, with identical sha256 across two runs. darwin-arm64 is `8a3a4fcc…`. `dist/manifest.json` is updated; there are no sidecars, so it has no `sidecars` array.
- Black-box selftest: 59/59 on darwin (4 runs) and 59/59 in each Linux container.
- An earlier linux-x64 run failed the K11 check (58/59). The emulator, not heimdall, writes `$HOME/.cache/rosetta`: `/bin/true` creates the same directory. The selftest now subtracts what a control program writes.
- Schema check: 23/23.
- The shared harness, run read-only for information only, reported 111/111.
